chunks: He said: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Muzaffar al-Bazzaz informed me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Abdul Malik ibn Ali al-Dahhan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Bashir, from As'ad ibn Sa'id, from Jabir who said:

Amirul Mu'mineen Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, heard a man insulting Qanbar, and Qanbar was about to respond to him. So Amirul Mu'mineen Ali, peace be upon him, called out to him: "Take it easy, O Qanbar! Leave the one who insults you in disgrace, and you will please the Most Merciful, anger Satan, and punish your enemy."
For by He Who split the grain and created the living soul, nothing from a believer pleases his Lord like forbearance, nothing angers Satan like silence, and the fool is best punished by ignoring him.

key_terms.الحلم: Hilm (forbearance/clemency) — the ability to remain composed and refrain from anger when provoked
key_terms.السكوت: Remaining quiet/ignoring — the act of deliberately not engaging with a fool
key_terms.الصمت: Silence — refraining from responding to provocation as a spiritual discipline
key_terms.النسمة: The breathing soul — a term for living beings in divine oath formulae
key_terms.شاتمك: The one who abuses/insults you — refers to verbal aggression

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about responding to insults and verbal abuse?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Mufid, Imam Ali (AS) instructs his devoted servant Qanbar to refrain from responding to a man who was verbally abusing him. The Imam teaches that restraint and silence in the face of insults simultaneously pleases God, angers Satan, and serves as the best punishment for the aggressor. This incident illustrates the practical application of forbearance (hilm) in daily life, a virtue highly valued in Islamic ethics.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abdul Husayn Muhammad ibnal-Muzaffar al-Bazzaz, reported to me from Abul Qasim Abdul Malik ibn ‘Ali al-Dahhan, who reported from Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn Bashir, from As’ad ibn Saeed from Jabir who said:

Once, Amirul Mu’mineen ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him heard someone abusing Qambar, and Qambar was about to answer back. So, Amirul Mu’mineen ‘Ali, peace be upon him, called out to Qambar: "Take it easy O, Qambar! Leave the one who abuses you to be ashamed of himself, so that Allah is pleased and Satan is resentful and your adversary is punished.

For, By He Who, split the grain and created the breathing man, nothing from a believer pleases His Sustainer better than forbearance; and nothing makes Satan more indignant than the silence; and the fool is best punished when totally ignored."
